title: Bella and Cosmo Find the Echo
markdown:
Folks said the air in Whispering Valley hummed with quiet wonders. Bella, a bunny as white as a fluffy cloud, had whiskers always twitching with fun. Cosmo, a corgi whose floppy ears could hear a ladybug sigh, wagged his tail like a happy metronome. They were always up for an adventure.

One evening, as the sun painted the sky in rosy swirls, they were getting ready for sleep. Fireflies blinked like sleepy little stars.

“Goodnight, Bella,” barked Cosmo, tail tapping the soft ground.

“Goodnight, Cosmo,” whispered Bella, munching a sweet clover.

Then, from far across the green valley, a soft sound drifted. “Goodnight, Cosmo. Goodnight, Bella.”

Bella’s pink ears popped up. “Did you hear that, Cosmo?” Her nose wiggled.

Cosmo tilted his head, ears flopping. “I did. It sounds like it’s saying it back. Like a game.”

The next night Bella tried. “Goodnight, valley,” she called, clear as a bell.

And back came the whisper. “Goodnight, valley.”

Cosmo nudged her. “It is a game. Let’s find out who it is. Adventure time.”

Bella’s eyes sparkled. “Yes. A twilight walk to find the echo.”

The idea made her heart do a little flutter-thump. Cosmo felt it too, a tiny wobble in his paws. The sun sank low. Clouds blushed. The valley edges grew soft and dim, like a cozy blanket. Cosmo’s tail gave a thoughtful twitch. What if it’s something new? A little shiver of thought, not of fear, but of brand-new excitement.

“Come on, Cosmo.” Bella nudged him. “We’ll stick together. Always.”

His tail wagged. “Okay, Bella. Together.”

They set off, paw in paw, as the twilight turned a soft purple. The air smelled of warm grass and sweet honeysuckle. The echo seemed to call from further in. They came to a little brook, gurgling happily over smooth stones, sparkling with the last sunlight. Happy splash. Sweet damp earth. Today the brook was a little wider.

Cosmo stopped. Tail paused mid-wag. He remembered a puddle that had been too deep, paws wet and cold. Now his paws felt big and clumsy on the grass. What if the log is slippery? A little thought wobbled. He felt a tiny bit shy about crossing.

Bella hopped closer, ears soft and reassuring. “It’s okay, Cosmo. Look.” She pointed with her nose. “There’s a log. A perfect little bridge.”

A sturdy log covered in green moss, lying right across. Like a path made just for them. Cosmo took a deep breath of sweet evening air. Bella hopped on first, white paws light as feathers.

“It’s strong. Come on. I’m right here.”

He looked at the safe log, then at her encouraging smile. One paw, then another. Firm. Safe. With a little hop he was across. He shook himself, not because he was wet, but because he felt so proud. His tail wagged again, a happy drumbeat. The echo seemed to cheer, a friendly whisper. “Goodnight. Goodnight.”

They walked on, deeper into the soft twilight, toward where the trees grew closer. Leaves whispered secrets. The ground crunched, a nice crinkly sound.

And then they found it. Not a monster. Not a fairy cave. Just a hollow log lying on its side like a sleepy giant. A perfectly round hole in one end, framed by soft moss.

Bella, curiosity bubbling, hopped up and peeked inside. “Hello.”

From the other side, clear as day: “Hello.”

Cosmo wiggled his nose and peeked too, tail wagging. “Who are you?”

“Who are you?” the echo answered.

Bella giggled, a little puff of happiness that tickled Cosmo’s ears. “It’s not a person. It’s the log. The sound goes in this end.” She nudged it, whiskers tickling the moss. “And then it bounces back out the other end. Like a bouncy ball for sounds.”

Cosmo’s tail thumped. “So when we say goodnight, the log says goodnight back. The log’s echo. Just a friendly sound.” He nudged Bella, warm fur brushing hers. “We found it. Our echo.”

They looked at each other. No mystery left to be scared of. As they turned for home the last twilight faded. Tiny stars, like scattered diamonds, began to twinkle. They walked hand-in-paw. They did not announce that friendship made any walk a discovery. They only paused once at the brook, Cosmo crossing the mossy log without stopping this time, and when the valley whispered goodnight they whispered it back, knowing exactly who was listening.
